clue.text: English not serious about working and saving money

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

blocks.note: E is the standard abbreviation for English
something comic is light-hearted rather than serious
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Someone earnest describes a sober, hard-working attitude to putting money aside.
explanation.walkthrough: The comic word wraps around the working word, and English stands in front.
explanation.definitionFit: An economic choice is a thrifty one, one that avoids waste and so saves cash.

clue.text: I brought in nothing in tins for Northern people

indicators.note: brought in means placed inside, here inside the tins

blocks.note: cans are tins
nada is Spanish-derived slang for nothing
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has packed nothing in tins for people in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: Two layers of insertion: the I goes in nothing, and the result goes in tins. NADA is informal slang for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Canadians live in Canada, the large country north of the United States.

clue.text: Sleep is a solid recommendation

blocks.note: first meaning: a short doze
second meaning: a racing tipster's strongest tip of the day

explanation.walkthrough: In British horse racing, a tipster's nap is the selection considered most likely to win.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a brief sleep and a horse-racing tip that is backed with confidence.

clue.text: The writer supports not interrupting further rare mammal

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so one word sits in the middle of another
in a down clue, a support sits underneath, so this piece comes last

blocks.note: more means further or additional
taken as written
the writer refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: An author backs a policy of not disturbing a scarce animal any further.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, a piece that supports another is written below it, so 'The writer' comes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Monotremes are egg-laying mammals such as the platypus and echidna, a very small and unusual group.

clue.text: Alter name when harassed in capital of Costa Rica? Note: in this style?

definitions.text: Alter name when harassed in capital of Costa Rica? Note: in this style?

indicators.note: harassed means troubled and flustered, so the letters are thrown into disorder
in places the jumbled letters inside the country's name

blocks.note: the first letter of the country's first word
these nine letters are rearranged
taken as written
N stands for note

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a renamed Costa Rica would be in a certain style.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled letters sit between C and RICA, with N added at the end. The whole clue also describes the answer: Costa Rica is a Central American nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Costa Rica lies on the isthmus between Mexico and South America, so its people and style are Central American.

clue.text: Small advance when penning good material for advert

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as sheep are shut in a pen

blocks.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small
an advance of money is a loan
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A modest cash advance pays for good stuff to put in an advertisement.
explanation.walkthrough: The loan holds the G, with S placed before it all.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchy slogan is the memorable phrase that forms the core copy of an advertising campaign.

clue.text: Blade, its furthest tip slicing through wooden pole

indicators.note: the furthest tip of a word is its very end letter
slicing through means cutting into the middle of the pole

blocks.note: a spar is a stout wooden pole, as on a ship
the final letter of the defining word

explanation.surface: A blade's point cuts through a wooden pole.
explanation.walkthrough: Blade does double duty: it is the definition, and its last letter goes inside SPAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A spear is a single slender shoot, as in a blade or spear of grass.

clue.text: Peculiar beach accommodating complete collection of objects

indicators.note: accommodating means giving room to, so the beach holds the other word

blocks.note: odd means peculiar
the sands are a beach
to end something is to complete it

explanation.surface: A strange beach holds a full set of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complete' is a verb here, meaning finish, not an adjective meaning whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds and ends are miscellaneous small items, a random assortment of bits and pieces.

clue.text: Nothing missed in current access points for mountains

indicators.note: missed means left out, so that letter is omitted

blocks.note: O looks like zero, nothing
anodes are electrodes where electric current flows in

explanation.surface: Nothing is lost among the points where electricity enters.
explanation.walkthrough: ANODES drops its O.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andes are the long mountain range running down western South America.

clue.text: Sister accepting work needed with fiancé? It's not really funny

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the sister takes the work inside

blocks.note: a nun is addressed as Sister
OP, short for opus, is a musical work
one's intended is the person one is engaged to marry

explanation.surface: A nun takes on a job that requires the help of her fiancé, an odd situation for a sister.
explanation.walkthrough: OP is the usual crossword abbreviation for opus, a work; 'needed with' simply joins the halves.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said after accidental wordplay, disclaiming any joke, so it means the remark was not meant to amuse.

clue.text: Church season less defiled after dismissing priest, an opportunist

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so the priest's letter is removed

blocks.note: Advent is the season of the church year before Christmas
something less defiled is cleaner, more pure
P is the abbreviation for priest, sent away from the purer word

explanation.surface: A church season becomes less spoiled once a priest is sent packing, says an opportunist.
explanation.walkthrough: P is a standard abbreviation for priest. 'An opportunist' is the definition, not part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An adventurer can mean someone who seeks fortune by risky or unscrupulous means, an opportunist.

clue.text: Property broker to say how old they are when admitted to hospital department

indicators.note: a patient admitted to a department goes inside it

blocks.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

blocks.clueFragment: to say how old they are
blocks.note: to state one's age is to say how old one is

explanation.surface: A house seller must declare patients' ages on admission to a ward.
explanation.walkthrough: STATE AGE goes inside ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate agent is someone who handles the sale and letting of houses for clients, a property broker.

clue.text: A capital group of players as well

blocks.note: taken as written
the London Symphony Orchestra, a band of players in the capital

explanation.surface: A band from the capital plays too.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital here is London, and the LSO is its famous symphony orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: Also is a synonym for as well, meaning in addition or too.

clue.text: Group of players heads for large, even imposing building

indicators.note: heads are the tops or fronts of things, so only leading letters are taken

blocks.note: the cast is the group of actors in a production
the opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A theatre company heads for a large, even grand venue.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle is a large fortified residence, a classic example of an imposing building.

clue.text: According to the inscription, large beehive houses 500

indicators.note: a building that houses something holds it inside

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for large
an apiary is a place where bees are kept
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: An inscription records a big beehive holding five hundred bees.
explanation.walkthrough: The apiary houses D, and L goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapidary describes something engraved on stone, so a lapidary style is that of a carved inscription; the adjective fits the phrase.

clue.text: Scientist: "Working Si chips totally gutted"

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are removed, leaving only the outside letters
working suggests being worked over or kneaded into a new shape

blocks.note: taken as written
only the first and last letters are kept

explanation.surface: A researcher reports that silicon chips that work have been completely destroyed.
explanation.walkthrough: Si is the chemical symbol for silicon, the stuff of computer chips.
explanation.definitionFit: A physicist is a scientist who studies matter and energy.

clue.text: Hurt, I came for treatment of joint pain?

indicators.note: treatment means being processed or handled, so the letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An injured patient explains why they came to the clinic.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheumatic is the adjective for rheumatism, a condition of aches and stiffness in the joints.

clue.text: This will show warmth? I'm suppressing most of triumphant comment

indicators.note: most of means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
suppressing means holding down or keeping in, so one part is enclosed by the other

blocks.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
'so there!' is a triumphant retort, here losing its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone smug about being warm-hearted holds back their gloating remark.
explanation.walkthrough: SO THERE loses its last E, and I'M is wrapped around what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: An isotherm is a line on a weather map joining places of equal temperature, so it shows how warm areas are.

clue.text: Unknown marvel not initially there

indicators.note: not at the start means the first letter is left off

blocks.note: Y is a classic algebraic unknown
a wonder is a marvel; its first letter is dropped

explanation.surface: An unknown marvel was not there at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonder is an old or dialect word meaning over there, at a distance.

clue.text: Furniture item found in thousands of apartments

indicators.note: found in says the answer is lying inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture turns up in thousands of flats.
explanation.definitionFit: A sofa is an upholstered seat for several people, a common item of furniture.

clue.text: Proposal not on, about to go belly-up

indicators.note: belly-up means turned upside down, so in a down entry the letters read upwards

blocks.note: something not on is off
RE means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A deal is cancelled, about to collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, belly-up means turned upside down, so RE reads upward.
explanation.definitionFit: An offer is a proposal put forward for someone to accept or reject.

clue.text: Notes, easily picked up, favouring development of mitosis

indicators.note: development means change or growth, so the letters take a new form

blocks.note: to be for something is to favour it
the letters of this biology term are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is keen on how cell division develops, with notes easy to take in.
explanation.walkthrough: Mitosis is cell division in biology, a red herring that sends the solver toward science.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortissimo music is played very loudly, so its notes are readily heard by any listener.

clue.text: Key point as we see it: King to be replaced by Catholic

indicators.note: replaced by says one letter swaps out for another

blocks.note: 'for us' means in our view
R, for rex, is a king; this letter goes out
C abbreviates Catholic and takes the king's place

explanation.surface: In our view, the central issue is a Catholic monarch replacing a king.
explanation.walkthrough: FOR US swaps its R for C.
explanation.definitionFit: A focus is the central point of attention, the main or key point.

clue.text: Insect found in Bordeaux, perhaps - it targets the legs

blocks.note: first meaning: a chirping insect in a French city, taken literally
second meaning: an informal garden game in which the batter's legs act as the wicket

explanation.walkthrough: French cricket is a children's garden version of cricket, a British bat-and-ball sport; the ball is bowled at the batter's legs instead of stumps.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally names a chirping bug in France and is also the name of a casual game aimed at the batter's shins.

clue.text: Parrot occupying lake area

indicators.note: occupying means sitting inside, so the bird lives within these words

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: A parrot is living near a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The kea is a large mountain parrot native to New Zealand.

clue.text: Assassin's track after boarding public transport

indicators.note: boarding a vehicle means getting inside it

blocks.note: a bus is a common form of public transport
a rut is a track worn into the ground

explanation.surface: A killer's trail is picked up after he gets on a bus.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the assassin to the wordplay; the rut boards the bus.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutus was one of the conspirators who stabbed Julius Caesar, history's best-known assassin.

clue.text: Fan to breed bird

blocks.note: a nut is an enthusiast, as in a fitness nut
to hatch young is to breed them

explanation.surface: A bird enthusiast wants to breed birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The nuthatch is a small songbird known for climbing down tree trunks head first.
